Work starts with defining the business question and data measures, proceeds through experience analysis, assumption selection, model calculations, and stress scenarios, then has others recalculate key results before delivering rate recommendations, reserve assessments, or risk reports. The difficulty often lies in whether data represent the target population, observation periods align, anomalies have business explanations, and outputs suit the current purpose, rather than in formulas themselves.
Retain inputs, assumptions, code, calculations, and review records; explain limitations first when observation periods or populations differ, without directly combining them into one risk conclusion.

BLS and O*NET support mathematics and statistics as task foundations; this page has no evidence of a uniform actuarial IQ threshold or score-based occupational performance predictions.

items.title: Official materials and editorial preparation suggestions

values: Fictional exercise inputs

The observation period is the same complete year; Group A has exposure of 1000 policy-years, 200 claims, and total losses of 400000 CNY; Group B has 500 policy-years, 150 claims, and total losses of 450000 CNY.
All data are editorially fictional. Counts refer to claim events; amounts use the same period and currency and exclude expenses, profit, or reserves.
Exposure is measured in policy-years, not the number of policies at year end.
Tasks and deliverables
Calculate frequency = count/exposure, severity = loss/count, and loss cost = loss/exposure separately; then calculate combined values.
Increase the combined portfolio's frequency by 10% with severity unchanged; separately increase severity by 10% with frequency unchanged. Produce a recalculation sheet and one page of limitations.
Reference recalculation
A: frequency 0.2 claims/policy-year, severity 2000 CNY/claim, and loss cost 400 CNY/policy-year. B: 0.3 claims/policy-year, 3000 CNY/claim, and 900 CNY/policy-year.
Combined: exposure 1500, count 350, and losses 850000 CNY; frequency 7/30 ≈ 0.233333, severity 17000/7 ≈ 2428.571429, and loss cost 1700/3 ≈ 566.666667.
Scenario loss cost when each factor is increased separately by 10%: 1870/3 ≈ 623.333333 CNY/policy-year; do not change both factors simultaneously.
Boundaries and self-checks
Not actual product rates, reserves, or investment advice. Single-period data are insufficient to identify trends, development factors, and product differences.
Check zero denominators, units, periods, and whether A/B group rates were incorrectly averaged; manual checking is possible without real customer data.

entries.answer: Typical work starts with organizing experience data and business conditions, proceeds through assumption selection, calculating loss or benefit-payment distributions, and testing model results, then produces pricing, reserve, or risk recommendations and explains limitations to management and relevant professionals.
entries.question: What do actuaries do every day?

entries.answer: Actuaries focus on long-term uncertainty, insurance liabilities, and funding adequacy; financial risk specialists focus more on market and investment risks, statisticians on general statistical inference, insurance underwriters on acceptance and terms of individual business, and bioinformatics technicians on life-science data processing.
entries.question: How do actuaries differ from adjacent occupations?

entries.answer: Observable fit signals include willingness to investigate data anomalies, explain why assumption changes affect rates or liabilities, repeatedly validate calculations, and explain technical results to colleagues who do not build models.
entries.question: How can I judge whether actuarial work suits me?

entries.answer: Software can accelerate data cleaning, scenario calculations, code generation, and result compilation, but entry into production processes depends on data permissions, reproducibility, model validation, and organizational governance.
entries.question: Which tasks will AI change?

entries.answer: Software can accelerate data cleaning, scenario calculations, code generation, and result compilation.
entries.question: Which actuarial tasks can AI assist with?

entries.answer: People with defined responsibilities must still review and explain whether assumptions fit business and regulatory contexts, how anomalous data are handled, and whether model results can support rate or reserve decisions, taking responsibility for escalation.
entries.question: Which stages must retain human review?

entries.answer: Currently verifiable precise occupational wage materials cover US actuaries and do not support claims about mainland Chinese actuaries' national occupational median, uniform starting pay, or individual take-home income.
entries.question: How should actuarial wages in mainland China be interpreted?

entries.answer: The median US actuarial annual wage in month 5 of 2025 was 130,000 USD; in that year's wage distribution, the lowest 10% earned below 78,570 USD and the highest 10% above 215,100 USD. These statistics describe employed workers' wages; the median is not starting pay for new entrants. Lower percentiles provide comparison references without promising individual entry wages.
entries.question: Does the US actuarial median wage represent entry-level income?

entries.answer: US occupational materials list a bachelor's degree as typical actuarial entry-level education and state that becoming a certified professional generally requires passing a series of examinations.
entries.question: What are the typical US actuarial education and examination pathways?

entries.answer: Actuarial examination progress and professional certification may provide evidence of abilities, while employers, professional organizations, and local rules jointly determine specific-role authorization, signing responsibilities, and regulated-business scope.
